title: Slice custody of the graph generation builders
description: Who may build the next graph generation at the same time. A builder announces the owners it is going to write (the stale projects of its plan) as a CLAIM, a closed document `<directory>/<token>.json` beside the generation documents (written by rename), and holds the exclusive lease `graph-custody:<root>:<token>` from before the document exists until it is removed; a claim whose lease is free belongs to a dead command and is removed by the next reader. A claim is `structural` when its write set cannot be named before the build (a cold generation, a stale environment, added or removed project configurations): it conflicts with every other claim. Two claims conflict when either is structural or their owner sets intersect. Every claim receives under the short admission lease `graph-custody-admission:<root>` a ticket one above the largest ticket of the live claims; a claim is `held` (may build) once no live claim that is held or has a smaller ticket conflicts with it, so disjoint refreshes build at the same time, overlapping ones build one after the other in ticket order, and a waiting claim is never overtaken by a later conflicting one (no starvation). A holder that finds more stale owners than it claimed extends its claim when no other held claim conflicts with the extension, else it gives the custody back and queues again with the union (at most `widenRounds` times, then structurally). Pointer publication checks its original claim against the handover grace under the admission lease. A released or deposed holder cannot publish an authoritative pointer. A holder retires old generation documents only when it can make its claim structural because no other live claim exists. Waiting is event driven (the leases of the blocking claims) with a poll of `pollMilliseconds`; a waiter tells why at most every `noticeMilliseconds`, naming up to `sampleOwners` shared owners. A reader whose stale projects a live claim already refreshes does not prepare them beside the builder: it ATTACHES (`attachToBuilderV1`), looks every `attachPollMilliseconds` at the custody and the generation pointer, tells each wave the builder publishes and, at most every `attachRecheckMilliseconds`, tries to be served from the generation published so far; it ends when no live claim holds the custody against it any more.

Holder.description: Who builds: the process that holds or queues a claim, written once with the claim so every waiter and the front door can say who is ahead. `digest` is the code identity the process runs (empty when unknown).

Progress.description: Sidecar `<token>.progress.json` of a held claim: the phase and owner counters of its build and the time of its last ADVANCE (the phase changed or `done` grew). A holder that does not advance for `stallMilliseconds` is asked to hand over; progress, not elapsed time, decides.

Ask.description: Sidecar `<token>.ask.json` written by a waiter: the holder is asked to stop at its next unit boundary, keep what it finished and release. `stalled`: no advance for `stallMilliseconds`; `stale-code`: the code digest of the holder differs from the current library. A holder that has not answered `askGraceMilliseconds` after `atMs` no longer blocks the door (it is deposed).
